days.reason: The entire Matthew 24 is the central text for Christ the King Sunday. The chapter describes the coming of the Son of Man on the clouds of heaven with power and glory (v. 30), the gathering of the elect (v. 31), the parables about being watchful and ready (vv. 32-51), and the final judgment. This is the main theme of the day, and the entire chapter should be marked as primary.

Advent has a dual perspective: waiting for Jesus' first coming and waiting for his return. The whole of Matthew 24 describes the signs of the end of the world, the call to endure, and exhortations to be watchful and ready (vv. 42-44). This is a central part of Advent's eschatological expectation and warning to stay awake. The chapter is often used as a reading on the first Sunday of Advent.

This chapter is the central text for Christ the King Sunday. The text describes the coming of the Son of Man on the clouds of heaven with power and glory (v. 30), the gathering of the elect (v. 31), and the final judgment over world history. This is the main theme of the day.

The verses contain the parable of the fig tree and exhortations to be watchful and ready because that day and hour are unknown. This is a central part of the message on Christ the King Sunday: the waiting period and expectation of Christ's return.

The parable of the faithful and the wicked servant illustrates the consequences of being prepared or unprepared when the Lord comes. This underscores the reality of judgment and the responsibility of believers, which is a central theme on Christ the King Sunday.

Advent has a dual perspective: waiting for Jesus' first coming and waiting for his return. Matt 24:1-14 describes the signs of the end of the world and the call to endure, which is part of Advent's eschatological expectation and warning to stay awake.

Exhortations to watch and be ready (vv. 42-44) are a classic Advent theme. The text reminds us that we await a Lord who comes at an unpredictable time, which defines the spiritual attitude of the Advent season.

_versions.reason: [minor] The tagging of Advent-1 is divided into two separate blocks (vv. 1–14 and vv. 36–44) with a large gap in between (vv. 15–35). Although vv. 15–35 deal with the great tribulation and the signs, there is a continuous eschatological expectation throughout the chapter that belongs to the Advent theme. It is better to have one cohesive tag for the entire chapter or at least most of its parts under Advent-1 to show the unity of the 'waiting time'. However, since vv. 15–31 are very specific about the 'signs' and the 'tribulation' before the return, it can be argued that there is a natural break. But for a day-tagging intended to capture the chapter's use in the liturgy, it is common to link the entire chapter to Advent-1 as a secondary reading, or at least those parts dealing with 'nearness' and 'watchfulness'. The current division is somewhat artificial. I would suggest expanding Advent-1 to cover the whole chapter (1–51) as secondary, or at least covering parts such as vv. 15–35 which also deal with 'nearness' (v. 33: 'he is near'). But to be strict about 'actual errors': It is not wrong to split it, but it is incomplete. I would suggest expanding Advent-1 to cover 1–51 to capture the entire chapter's Advent perspective, or at least 1–35. Let us look at verse 33: 'So also you, when you see all these things, know that he is near and stands at the door.' This is a central Advent theme. Therefore, Advent-1 should cover 1–35 or 1–51. The current tagging lacks 15–35 under Advent-1.; [minor] The tagging of Last Sunday is divided into three parts. This is not wrong in itself, but it is unnecessary to split it into three separate objects with the same 'primary' relevance for the whole chapter. It is more correct to have one single tag for the entire chapter (1–51) with 'primary' relevance, since the whole chapter is a continuous discourse about the return and judgment. The division into 1–31, 32–44, and 45–51 creates an illusion that these parts are independent, whereas they form one cohesive unit. It is better to have one tag for the entire chapter.; [minor] As mentioned above, Advent-1 lacks tagging for verses 15–35. This is an important part of the chapter dealing with the 'signs' and the 'nearness' of the return, which is central to Advent. It should be included.
